sections.heading: Return Definition
sections.body: A planetary return occurs when a transiting planet returns to its natal position. Treat the return chart as a cycle map for that planet's topics: closure of one cycle, beginning of the next, and a concentrated preview of how that planet will operate until the next return.

sections.heading: Planet-Specific Scope
sections.body: Each return speaks through its planet. Solar returns emphasize vitality, identity, visibility, and annual direction. Lunar returns emphasize emotional climate and monthly movement. Mercury returns emphasize decisions, communication, study, commerce, travel, and logistics. Venus returns emphasize love, money, pleasure, aesthetics, and social ease. Mars returns emphasize action, conflict, stamina, risk, enterprise, and the body. Jupiter and Saturn returns describe larger multi-year developmental arcs.

sections.heading: Read Like A Chart
sections.body: Read the return chart as a chart, but keep the return planet central. Prioritize the return Ascendant, angular planets, the return planet's house and aspects, house rulers, repeated natal themes, and close contacts to natal planets or angles.

sections.heading: Timing With Transits
sections.body: The return chart describes the cycle; later transits to the return chart can time when its promises become active. This is especially useful for solar, lunar, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn return cycles.

sections.heading: Retrograde Return Series
sections.body: Retrograde planets can create more than one return in a short span. Treat a three-pass return as a sequence: first contact introduces the cycle issue, retrograde contact reviews or reverses it, final direct contact commits the outcome or direction.

sections.heading: Do Not Overpromise
sections.body: A return chart does not guarantee a single event. It gives a cycle field. Raise confidence only when the return chart repeats natal promise, progression, active transit, or time-lord testimony.
